column1: Fragile by Design|2014|0|10||8.5,9,8.5,8.5,8,9,8,9,7.5,8|Charles W. Calomiris and Stephen H. Haber|Comparative historical explanation of banking systems through political coalitions, regulation and credit allocation. https://business.columbia.edu/faculty/research/fragile-design-political-origins-banking-crises-and-scarce-credit verifies 2014 and five-country comparison. Institutional bargains offer a causal framework, but selected cases do not establish that politics explains every banking failure. D=8 low confidence from contents, author interview and attributed review extracts; country contrasts add constraints rather than mere repetition. Finance/politics T12; multinational scope avoids T11, broad cross-period account H13=0. Not a banking technical manual.

The Origins of Value|2005|0|10||8.5,8,7.5,8,8,9,8,9,7,8|William N. Goetzmann and K. Geert Rouwenhorst, editors|Historical essays on financial instruments, trade, monetary media and institutions; not a technical reference for pricing securities. https://academic.oup.com/book/52333 verifies editors and 2005; https://natlib.govt.nz/records/21982139 lists distinct cases and references 359–394 of 404 numbered pages. D=8 low confidence from contents: varied instruments add mechanisms and historical knowledge, anthology organization may weaken cumulative argument. Financial innovation T12 applies despite innovation fit; global and cross-period, T11/H13=0.

The End of Theory|2017|0|10||7.5,8,8,8,7.5,8,8.5,8.5,7.5,7|Richard Bookstaber|Argument for agent-based models, endogenous crisis dynamics and attention to radical uncertainty, not a coding or modeling course. https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvc776sc and https://assets.press.princeton.edu/catalogs/S17AcadTrade.pdf establish 2017 and purpose. Strong practical perspective, but superiority of the proposed approach is not treated as a proven cure for crises; broad dismissal of standard models lowers E. D=7.5 low confidence from contents/description and review extracts; distinct modeling limits add learning, prescriptions remain less substantiated. Finance T12; international mechanism focus T11=0, H13=0.

A Demon of Our Own Design|2007|10|10|2006|8,8.5,8.5,8.5,8,9,8.5,9,8,7.5|Richard Bookstaber|Insider account of leverage, liquidity feedback, tight coupling and institutional risk failures. https://obnb.uk/p13612933-a-demon-of-our-own-design-markets-hedge-funds-and-the-perils-of-financial-innovation verifies original 2007 and chapter structure. Case detail supports transferable mechanisms but first-person attribution remains partial. D=8 low-confidence contents/description estimate; distinct crises expose different constraints, personal/institutional detail may be lower-yield. US financial institutions predominate in narrative and influence, so both T11 and T12 apply. Approximate central period ends 2006; not updated to include the later global crisis.

Irrational Exuberance|2000|10|10||8.5,8,8,8,8,9,7.5,9.5,8,8|Robert J. Shiller|Empirical and behavioral account of speculative feedback, narratives and valuation, not an investment-training course. https://assets.press.princeton.edu/chapters/s7922.pdf provides a sampled opening chapter and https://www.econ.yale.edu/~shiller/data.htm underlying data. Original 2000 confirmed by https://assets.press.princeton.edu/about_pup/PUP100/book/8gShiller.pdf . Do not infer universal predictive accuracy from one successful warning. D=8 low confidence from sample and structure; long-run data and social mechanisms add distinct learning. US asset markets dominate case base, T11; finance T12. Recurring mechanism across cycles H13=0, rather than assigning endpoint from one market peak.

Tulipmania|2007|10|10|1637|9,7,7,7.5,7,9,5.5,9,7,8|Anne Goldgar|Archival reconstruction of Dutch tulip trading and reputational trust that tests familiar bubble stories. https://pressblog.uchicago.edu/2007/05/23/press-release-goldgar-tulipmania.html and https://guides.loc.gov/business-booms-busts/tulip-mania establish the revisionist scope; https://library.daystar.ac.ke/bib/94058 gives contents and references 327–397 of 425 numbered pages. D=7 low confidence from contents and description; contract and social-network evidence adds learning, specialist local detail may have lower yield. National economic history and finance trigger both penalties; central episode ends 1637, H13 capped. Distinct from Mike Dash's Tulipomania.

Paper Promises|2011|0|10||7.5,8,7.5,7.5,7,7,7.5,8,8,7.5|Philip Coggan|History and analysis of debt, currency regimes and distributional conflict, not a trading manual. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL17911393W/Paper_promises and https://obnb.uk/a00321196-philip-coggan verify 2011, not the 2012 US or 2013 paperback edition. https://www.hachette.co.uk/titles/philip-coggan/paper-promises/9781610392297/ outlines the argument; strong predictions of creditor-led geopolitical change remain dated forecasts rather than current facts, reducing R. D=7 low confidence from contents/description; monetary regime comparisons supply payload, current-affairs framing has lower lasting yield. Finance T12, multinational T11=0; broad monetary history H13=0.

Golden Fetters|1992|0|10|1939|9,9,8.5,9,8,9.5,8.5,9.5,7,8|Barry Eichengreen|Sustained historical causal argument on monetary constraints, international transmission and policy response, not a technical economics curriculum. https://www.nber.org/books-and-chapters/golden-fetters-gold-standard-and-great-depression-1919-1939 establishes original 1992 and argument. Comparative timing of monetary exits and constraints provides reusable institutional mechanisms; no claim that gold alone explains every dimension of the Depression. D=8 low confidence from description and chapter structure; country comparisons add boundary conditions, detailed monetary chronology may be less efficient. T12 finance, global scope T11=0; explicit historical endpoint 1939.
